cases.title: Eagle Avenue Lift Bridge
cases.summary: The two exposed counterweights, freestanding braced towers and narrow mast over the span form a distinctive match between the film and a separately labeled historical photograph. The evidence identifies the bridge visible in frames 638 and 652; it does not locate the camera or the gravel pile precisely.

frames.caption: Frame 652 gives the clearest combined view of both braced lift towers, their broad rectangular counterweights and the thin mast between them.
frames.alt: Frame 652 gives the clearest combined view of both braced lift towers, their broad rectangular counterweights and the thin mast between them.

frames.caption: Frame 638 shows one braced tower and its exposed counterweight behind Tank on the gravel pile. Compare its structure with the wider view in frame 652.
frames.alt: Frame 638 shows one braced tower and its exposed counterweight behind Tank on the gravel pile. Compare its structure with the wider view in frame 652.

references.caption: The source independently labels this as the Eagle Street lift bridge. The exposed counterweights, open braced towers and central lattice mast are the features used in this comparison. The photograph is taken from a vessel at a different angle.
references.alt: Black and white view of the Eagle Street lift bridge from a vessel, showing the truss span, exposed counterweights at the towers and a narrow mast above the span.

observations.title: Paired towers and counterweights
observations.text: Frame 652 shows two tall, freestanding steel towers with open diagonal bracing and unusually broad, exposed rectangular counterweights. The labeled reference has the same arrangement. This combination carries more identifying weight than the general industrial setting.

observations.title: The narrow mast between the towers
observations.text: A thin lattice mast rises above the span in both frame 652 and Figure XIII, with lines extending toward the towers. It adds a second, spatially related feature to the tower comparison.

observations.title: A link between two film views
observations.text: The braced tower and broad counterweight behind Tank in frame 638 are consistent with the clearer pair in frame 652. The identification applies to these visible structures; adjacent cuts in the sequence still need their own evidence.

uncertainties: The historical photograph's capture date and individual photographer are not specified in the chapter. The 1981 date belongs to the book, and 2016 belongs to the digital edition.
The film and reference use different viewpoints. Neither the precise camera station nor the gravel-pile parcel is established.
The map point marks the bridge as a landmark. It does not trace Tank's route or assign every nearby industrial insert to this site.
cases.resolution: Retain Eagle Avenue Lift Bridge as a strong landmark identification for frames 638 and 652. A period site plan or aerial tied to the film's sight lines would be needed to locate the gravel pile and camera more precisely.

cases.title: Madison Square Building, Hough Avenue
cases.summary: Frame 63 shows MADISON roof lettering on a long brick apartment and shop building with pale corner blocks, stacked balconies and a tall central arch. The city inventory and a dated Hough/East 79th photograph support Madison Square as the candidate, while the full facade remains unverified.

frames.caption: Frame 63: MADISON is legible along the roofline; possible SQUARE lettering is less clear. The central arch, stacked balconies, pale corner blocks and corner storefront are the features to compare.
frames.alt: Frame 63: MADISON is legible along the roofline; possible SQUARE lettering is less clear. The central arch, stacked balconies, pale corner blocks and corner storefront are the features to compare.

observations.title: A named architectural candidate
observations.text: The film's MADISON lettering is unusually useful. The long brick elevation, pale corner blocks, stacked balconies and central arch provide several features that a complete historical facade photograph could test together.

observations.title: Partial corner correspondence
observations.text: The 1964 photograph independently fixes a drugstore corner at Hough Avenue and East 79th Street. Its pale corner blocks and Coca-Cola cornice support the comparison with frame 63, but the reference includes only a narrow part of the candidate building.

observations.title: An address record with a defined limit
observations.text: The Cleveland Landmarks Commission inventory lists Madison Square Building at 7812–14 Hough Avenue, built in 1915 and demolished. Apartment-building directories from 1943–44 and 1955 instead list Madison Square at 7820 Hough Avenue. The records support a named Hough Avenue candidate while leaving the entrance or address-range relationship unresolved.

observations.title: Later block context
observations.text: The 1972 aerial helps place the intersection within the surrounding blocks. It should be read with its date and oblique angle in mind when comparing it with the film's street-level view.

uncertainties: A source photograph showing the central arch, the entire balcony pattern and the roof lettering together has not yet been matched.
The municipal inventory's 7812–14 Hough address and the apartment directories' 7820 Hough address have not been reconciled to a single entrance or parcel range.
The SQUARE portion of the film's roof lettering is less legible than MADISON in the available 480 × 270 still.
The corner photograph dates to 1964 and the aerial to 1972; neither is a documented film-production photograph.
The existing pin is an approximate Hough/East 79th vicinity reference, not the demolished building footprint or a camera position. Frames 58–62 remain unassigned.
cases.resolution: Keep the identification probable. The decisive next evidence is a dated full facade view or a building drawing tying the central arch, balconies and roofline to Madison Square's documented Hough Avenue address.

cases.title: Former Clark Avenue Bridge and furnace views
cases.summary: The final road-bridge views fit the former Clark Avenue crossing more plausibly than the earlier West 3rd Street label. The through-truss framework and documented furnace setting support that candidate, but the available references do not reproduce the film's road-level angle. The candidate remains unpinned.

frames.caption: Frame 658: a long road through-truss with repeated rounded or haunched inner portals, dense overhead lattice bracing and distant chimneys. This is the key unresolved bridge view.
frames.alt: Frame 658: a long road through-truss with repeated rounded or haunched inner portals, dense overhead lattice bracing and distant chimneys. This is the key unresolved bridge view.

observations.title: The road view that needs a match
observations.text: Frame 658 shows repeated inner portal frames with curved or haunched corners and a heavy lattice of diagonal members overhead. A road-level historical photograph must reproduce this structure and its relationship to the roadway before the bridge can be treated as confirmed.

observations.title: Compatible structure, incomplete angle
observations.text: The 1984 county photograph documents a high road through-truss with dense bracing. It is compatible with the candidate, but its low viewpoint and demolition state leave the film's portal sequence untested.

observations.title: Correcting the tall structure in frame 654
observations.text: The close view shows industrial piping and furnace equipment alongside grouped stacks. This feature belongs to the furnace complex and cannot serve as evidence for a lift-bridge tower.

observations.title: A documented industrial setting
observations.text: The 1935 archive caption places Republic Steel furnaces beside Clark Avenue Bridge. It supports the general setting of the candidate. The different date and view do not identify the film's exact furnace, steel-company parcel or camera station.

uncertainties: No equivalent road-level historical view has yet matched the full portal profile, span rhythm and skyline in frame 658.
The 1984 structural photograph records demolition well after the film; removed or changed elements limit direct comparison.
The film's precise camera stations, furnace identity and steel-company parcel remain unresolved.
The transition from Eagle Avenue in frame 652 to the furnace views does not by itself establish a continuous route or shared shooting position. Other ore-yard inserts retain their separate status.
cases.resolution: Retain former Clark Avenue Bridge as probable and withdraw West 3rd Street as the leading attribution. Keep this candidate unpinned until a period roadway photograph or engineering view aligns the inner portals, span sequence, roadway edge and industrial skyline.

researchNotes.topic: Madison Square: the full facade and an address variant
researchNotes.checked: Checked the CPL Madison catalog results, selected Hough/East 79th metadata and six additional photographs: two 1957 aerials, two 1966 street views, and two 1968 Hough/East 78th records showing the same scene. Also inspected the printed 1943–44 and 1955 apartment-directory pages and verified their parent volumes.
researchNotes.found: None of those photographs supplies the complete roofline, central arch and balcony arrangement needed for a full facade match. Frank Aleksandrowicz’s July 25, 1966 Hough/East 79th night view shows a partial balcony frontage at the left, with glare and cropping. Both directory scans list Madison Square at 7820 Hough Avenue, while the municipal inventory uses 7812–14.
researchNotes.remaining: Keep Madison probable. Reconcile the addresses using a parcel map, permit or building plan, then seek a full elevation or dated facade photograph. The Cleveland Press finding aid names Hough houses/buildings and streets/airviews folders; this focused online check did not exhaust those holdings.

researchNotes.topic: Leader Drug and Kronheim: specific archive folders, no confirmed pairing
researchNotes.checked: Re-inspected film frames 151 and 169 against CPL’s July 11, 1960 East 9th/St. Clair Leader Drug photograph. Checked the Cleveland Press digital catalog for Kronheim and Leader Drug, then verified the library’s original photograph-collection finding aid.
researchNotes.found: The 1960 photograph gives a definite Leader Drug branch, but the film’s night view still leaves the storefront geometry unresolved. The Kronheim catalog search returned an association portrait and two Euclid Avenue parade records; it did not establish the film pairing. More usefully, the finding aid lists separate Kronheim Furniture Co. and Leader Drug Stores folders in collection PH2000.000PRE, Subjects series, ca. 1920–1982, printed p.29.
researchNotes.remaining: The folder index supplies no specific photograph dates, addresses, box numbers or evidence of neighboring stores. Examine those folders or a 1967–68 business/street directory for a Leader Drug and furniture frontage that fit the same block. The 1955 Kronheim address at 2041 East 55th remains an earlier lead, and the film scene stays unplaced.
